expected_behavior: Public candidate audit reports zero findings for the new lifecycle contract documents.
actual_behavior: The first audit reported credential_assignment for a prose acceptance criterion in 00_STAGE_CONTRACT.md.
security_impact: No credential or private value was present; closeout remained blocked until the public audit returned zero findings.
root_cause: The prose used an assignment-shaped phrase with the scanner keyword authorization followed by a colon and a non-placeholder value.
attempted_fixes: Rephrased the acceptance criterion as a complete sentence without assignment syntax.
Reran the exact public candidate audit.

expected_behavior: The full deterministic suite passes while all test temporary data remains on the D drive.
actual_behavior: The first D-drive full-suite run reported 6 failures: five identity tests rejected repository-local tmp_path values outside .private, and one evidence CLI test did not redact a repository-local .tmp source as external.
security_impact: No product boundary was bypassed and no secret was exposed. The run command placed security-sensitive test fixtures in a location that the existing application correctly rejects.
reproduction_commands: Set TEMP, TMP, and --basetemp to D:/documents/agent/RAG_try/.tmp/lifecycle/g0-full-20260726-01 and run python -m pytest -q.
root_cause: Moving pytest temporary files from an external OS temp root into repository-local .tmp changed their trust classification. Settings accepts repository-local identity files only below .private, while the evidence CLI intentionally redacts .private as external evidence.
attempted_fixes: Preserved the failed log and status hashes.
Reran with TEMP, TMP, and --basetemp below repository-local .private/lifecycle so data stayed on D while satisfying the existing private-path contract.

expected_behavior: Repeated deterministic full rebuilds under one frozen configuration produce one artifact-set hash.
actual_behavior: The first GREEN attempt produced two artifact-set hashes across two runs although embedding and corpus inputs were deterministic.
security_impact: None. Without correction, benchmark provenance would incorrectly classify timestamp variation as artifact nondeterminism.
reproduction_commands: Run tests/indexing/test_full_rebuild_measurement.py without passing the same builder started_at to both repetitions.
root_cause: The current ingestion contract writes the build ingestion timestamp into DocumentRecord and documents.json. The test allowed datetime.now to vary between repetitions.
attempted_fixes: Froze one builder timestamp across all repetitions while retaining separate observed wall-clock timestamps.
Recorded the frozen timestamp in every measurement row.
Confirmed one artifact-set hash in all four formal configurations.

actual_behavior: The first post-closeout validation returned ValidationError because the REQ-LC-002 CSV row contained one extra empty column.
attempted_fixes: Parsed handoff and traceability independently while emitting only error locations and types.
Removed the extra delimiter and verified that load_traceability returned seven rows.
Regenerated every affected prefix anchor and artifact hash before rerunning integrated validation.
expected_behavior: The final G2 traceability projection parses into exactly the frozen nine-column schema and the integrated lifecycle validator passes.
root_cause: A manual edit used three commas between test_ids and evidence_ids instead of two, creating an unnamed tenth CSV field and shifting the evidence ID into status.
security_impact: No source content or secret was exposed and no product behavior changed. Gate closeout remained blocked until the final evidence object validated.

actual_behavior: The first HTML GREEN attempt returned an empty body after a link element and reported 5 passed, 1 failed.
attempted_fixes: Separated ignored HTML void elements from paired suppressed active elements.
Added regression coverage for remote link, script, image attributes, and malformed active-element nesting.
Replaced integer suppression depth with a matched tag stack.
expected_behavior: HTML fallback extracts visible body text while ignoring remote and active elements.
root_cause: The extractor treated link as a paired suppressed element even though HTML defines it as a void element, so suppression never ended.
security_impact: No remote resource was loaded and no content escaped suppression. Legitimate visible HTML text was unavailable, so the Gate remained blocked.

actual_behavior: The first encoding-hardening run quarantined a valid ISO-8859-1 8-bit body and reported 29 passed, 1 failed.
attempted_fixes: Inspected stdlib message defects, display payload, and decoded payload separately.
Changed 7bit, 8bit, and binary handling to consume byte-preserving get_payload(decode=True) output before charset decoding.
Added an encoded non-ASCII subject and 8-bit body regression.
expected_behavior: A bounded EML with a valid declared non-UTF-8 charset is admitted and parsed without lossy byte conversion.
root_cause: The stdlib display string replaced a non-UTF-8 byte, while the byte-preserving decoded payload still contained the exact original byte. The first implementation re-encoded the lossy display string.
security_impact: No content or identity leaked. A legitimate mail was rejected, so availability and format support were below contract.

actual_behavior: Read-only security review found that the first staged-to-quarantine transition mutated payload and receipt files in place through several non-atomic operations.
attempted_fixes: Replaced in-place mutation with a complete private incoming quarantine object.
Fsynced payload, original receipt, and new receipt before one directory publication.
Added staged supersession when a quarantine twin exists.
Added failure injection before publication and after publication before staged cleanup.
expected_behavior: Any quarantine transition failure leaves either the original valid staged object or a complete quarantine object that makes stale staging ineligible.
root_cause: The original transition renamed payload and receipts inside the staged directory before publishing the final quarantine directory, so an injected filesystem error could interrupt the sequence.
security_impact: The risk was found before Gate acceptance. No source content leaked and no index state changed. The old design could have required manual recovery and therefore blocked G4 closeout.

actual_behavior: The first post-review focused run reported 18 failures because every stored receipt containing a canonical JSON timestamp was rejected during event inventory.
attempted_fixes: Grouped the failures by their shared child_admission_failure result.
Traced the first storage exception to strict validation of a Python dictionary.
Changed the receipt loader to validate canonical JSON bytes directly with model_validate_json.
Retained exact canonical-byte and expected-status checks.
Reran the focused set with 48 passing tests.
expected_behavior: Canonical stored receipts round-trip through the strict receipt model while non-canonical or tampered bytes remain rejected.
root_cause: The inventory decoded receipt JSON into a Python dictionary before calling a strict model. In strict Python mode an ISO timestamp string is not a datetime, although the same string is the required JSON representation.
security_impact: No boundary was bypassed and no content leaked. Valid attachment processing was unavailable, so G4 remained blocked.

actual_behavior: A root admitted under a broader G3 limit was fully read into memory before a stricter G4 max_message_bytes policy returned message_size_limit.
attempted_fixes: Selected deterministic root size reasons from the receipt before MIME parsing.
Added a regression that makes read_staged fail if called for a known-over-limit root.
Refactored quarantine payload transfer into 1 MiB chunks with byte-count and SHA-256 verification.
Reran focused, ingestion, related, and full regressions.
expected_behavior: A root known to exceed the runtime EML limit is quarantined without being fully allocated or passed to BytesParser.
root_cause: The entry point used max(configured_limit, receipt.byte_count) as the read bound and performed the stricter policy comparison only after read_staged returned.
security_impact: The final disposition was fail-closed, but a large admitted email could consume more memory than the current G4 policy intended. No MIME execution, index mutation, or content disclosure occurred.

actual_behavior: Review found that a storage error while quarantining a previously published child could abort failure handling before the root received its quarantine disposition.
attempted_fixes: Changed failure order to publish the root quarantine first.
Added active parent-chain validation to every staged child read.
Allowed child quarantine cleanup to validate its own bytes after the parent is quarantined.
Injected child cleanup failure and asserted the root remains quarantined and the residual child cannot be read.
expected_behavior: Any fail-closed parse makes the root and all descendants non-parseable even when physical descendant cleanup fails.
root_cause: The original cleanup sequence attempted child transitions before the authoritative root transition, so a child storage exception could interrupt the sequence.
security_impact: The issue was caught before G4 acceptance. A failed parse could otherwise leave its root staged and eligible for a later retry despite incomplete descendant cleanup.

actual_behavior: Independent review showed that a path-based attachment parser could observe replacement bytes between the pre-parse and post-parse staged hash checks, then the original file could be restored before the second check.
attempted_fixes: Added an immutable-byte method to ParserRegistry and every default text, HTML, CSV, JSONL, PDF, and DOCX parser.
Bound the exact bytes to the staged child receipt SHA-256 before dispatch.
Kept the post-dispatch staged integrity check as storage monitoring rather than parse provenance.
Added a regression that replaces and restores the staged file while parsing and proves the parsed text came from the receipt-bound bytes.
expected_behavior: The parser observes exactly the immutable bytes whose SHA-256 is stored in the child receipt.
root_cause: The first design verified a path twice but allowed the parser to reopen that mutable path between checks. Two valid endpoint hashes do not identify the bytes observed by an operation between them.
security_impact: A parsed attachment result could have been inconsistent with provenance and could have carried replacement text into indexing. The issue was found and fixed before G4 acceptance.

actual_behavior: Independent review found that two concurrent child admissions could both read the same remaining event file or byte budget and then both publish.
attempted_fixes: Added a lock file whose name is the SHA-256 of the event ID.
Used native msvcrt locking on Windows and flock on POSIX.
Held the lock across parent revalidation, event inventory, budget checks, child copy, classification, and publication.
Added a synchronized two-thread regression that proves only one child spends the final event slot.
expected_behavior: Event-wide child count and byte budgets are atomically checked and consumed across threads and service processes sharing the asset store.
root_cause: The inventory read and later publication were separate operations without a shared event-scoped critical section.
security_impact: Concurrent work could exceed a configured event asset budget. Identity and type validation still applied, but resource governance could be bypassed.

actual_behavior: Independent review demonstrated that default serialization of an unencoded nested EML changed CRLF to LF, reducing the child byte count and producing a receipt hash for a rewritten representation.
attempted_fixes: Created a dedicated nested EML serialization policy with CRLF line endings and source-header refolding disabled.
Applied the attachment limit to that preserved byte representation.
Added a fixture whose limit lies between the shortened LF form and the CRLF witness.
Asserted accepted child byte count and SHA-256 equal the CRLF nested witness.
expected_behavior: An unencoded nested EML cannot become smaller through parser serialization before byte-budget accounting and receipt hashing.
root_cause: email.policy.default serializes with LF and may refold source headers, while the first child budget used len(nested.as_bytes(default)).
security_impact: A crafted nested message could consume more source bytes than the child budget and weaken exact provenance. No external execution or index mutation occurred during the review.

actual_behavior: Independent review found that max_output_chars counted only body.text and attachment parsed.text while subject, addresses, date, warnings, sections, tables, metadata, and locators also appeared in returned models.
attempted_fixes: Added recursive accounting of every returned textual value in ParseResult and mail metadata.
Applied accounting during preflight before child publication where possible.
Added a long-subject regression and adjusted the attachment structured-output regression to preserve reason precedence.
expected_behavior: Attacker-controlled textual values returned by the parser consume one monotonic output budget across the complete nested parse.
root_cause: The first budget treated ParseResult.text as the entire output although the typed result repeats or adds structured textual fields.
security_impact: Bounded individual fields prevented unbounded output, but aggregate returned text could exceed the configured limit.

actual_behavior: Independent review could deserialize a parsed outcome with decoded_child_bytes set to zero or the same child referenced twice; a later local review also found mime_part_count could be changed without rejection.
attempted_fixes: Required parsed decoded_child_bytes to equal the sum of child receipt byte counts.
Required quarantined decoded_child_bytes to cover every published child.
Rejected duplicate attachment or nested-message references.
Stored the MIME subtree count on ParsedEmailMessage and required exact root outcome equality.
Added model-validation regressions for each contradiction.
expected_behavior: A serialized EmailParseOutcome cannot claim false MIME or byte counts and cannot represent one child more than once in the parsed tree.
root_cause: The original model checked set coverage and basic status shape but did not compare accounting fields with the typed child tree.
security_impact: Runtime construction was correct, but a persisted or API-deserialized outcome could have produced misleading audit counters and lineage.

actual_behavior: Independent review found that the allowlisted public trace exposed the root content SHA-256, allowing equal content to be correlated across tenants or a known candidate mail to be confirmed.
attempted_fixes: Removed root_content_sha256 from EmailPublicTrace.
Updated the allowlist regression to require that the private receipt hash is absent from serialized trace.
Updated the G4 contract, ADR, results, and learning guide.
expected_behavior: A public-safe trace contains operational counts and pseudonymous identifiers without a stable fingerprint of private content.
root_cause: The first allowlist classified a cryptographic hash as harmless metadata without considering cross-tenant equality and dictionary confirmation.
security_impact: No body text was directly disclosed, but the fingerprint enabled content correlation. It was removed before G4 acceptance.

actual_behavior: The first catalog validator required materialization before consulting the persisted ledger, so a valid same-event replay after restart failed with materialization_required instead of returning the original revision.
attempted_fixes: Moved the materialization-required decision after SourceEventLedger.apply.
Allowed replay to omit materialization while requiring any supplied replay materialization to equal the accepted provenance.
Added restart and byte-exact no-rewrite regression coverage.
expected_behavior: A persisted same-event same-payload replay reuses the authoritative revision without rerunning parsing or rewriting the catalog.
root_cause: A new-UPSERT precondition was applied before the durable ledger could distinguish APPLIED from REPLAYED.
security_impact: No event was duplicated, but restart idempotency was unavailable and callers could have retried unnecessary parsing work.

actual_behavior: Path.exists returned false for a dangling catalog symlink, so the first loader could have interpreted the redirected entry as an uninitialized empty catalog.
attempted_fixes: Replaced follow-link existence checks with lstat-based entry checks.
Required catalog, lock, anchor, and managed temporary entries to be regular, single-link, non-reparse files.
Added dangling-link and hardlink regressions with an explicit platform skip where symlink creation is unavailable.
expected_behavior: Any catalog path entry, including a dangling symlink or reparse point, fails closed rather than becoming an empty catalog.
root_cause: Path.exists follows links and reports a dangling link as absent, which is not the required filesystem-entry question.
security_impact: On a platform and directory where an untrusted subject could create that link, idempotency and ownership state could have failed open to an empty snapshot.

actual_behavior: Strict model reconstruction accepted a source lineage whose root was DELETE, accepted DELETE after a tombstone, and did not compare a historical revision region with its persisted receipt.
attempted_fixes: Required every source lineage root to be UPSERT.
Required DELETE to have a live parent and inherit both region and ACL.
Compared every revision region with its matching receipt, not only the current head.
Added direct deserialization tests for impossible histories.
expected_behavior: Recovery input must reject every revision graph that the G2 runtime state machine could never produce.
reproduction_commands: python -m pytest tests/ingestion/test_revision_catalog.py -k 'root_delete or delete_after_tombstone or historical_region' -q
root_cause: The initial snapshot validator relied on normal SourceEventLedger.apply behavior without fully restating those semantic invariants at the untrusted persistence boundary.
security_impact: Normal API calls could not produce the state, but a malformed or rewritten persistence artifact could have loaded misleading deletion and governance history.

actual_behavior: The first ChangePlan allowed a non-empty base without a base index run, allowed base and target to share one run ID, treated parser or normalizer changes as governance-only, and recorded exclusions only by source identity.
attempted_fixes: Bound base and target event counts to base-index requirements and distinct immutable run IDs.
Added materialization_changed and revision_only classifications before governance-only fallback.
Bound each exclusion to event ID, canonical payload hash, tenant, source, and one disposition.
Included accepted and excluded attempt payload hashes in the deterministic source-event digest.
expected_behavior: An executable plan identifies a distinct immutable target, carries enough event provenance to reproduce exclusions, and cannot hide parser or normalizer invalidation.
root_cause: The first plan was a source-head diff but did not yet encode downstream immutable-run and cache-invalidation preconditions.
security_impact: A later incremental builder could have received an apparently executable plan that encouraged same-run overwrite or incorrect compute reuse.

actual_behavior: An exception after atomic replacement was reported as catalog_publish_failed even though the new event could already be authoritative; retry then returned REPLAYED.
attempted_fixes: Tracked the atomic replacement boundary explicitly.
Kept catalog_publish_failed for confirmed pre-replace failures.
Introduced catalog_commit_outcome_unknown for directory-sync, anchor, or verification failure after replacement.
Required same-event idempotent retry and added both sync and read-verification fault injection.
expected_behavior: The error contract distinguishes definitely-not-committed from commit-outcome-unknown so callers retry safely by event ID.
root_cause: The first publication exception handler collapsed failures on both sides of the linearization point into one code.
security_impact: The bytes remained complete, but an operator could not know whether a compensating action or an idempotent retry was correct.

actual_behavior: A missing authoritative catalog was always treated as first initialization, an older internally valid catalog was accepted, existing directory permissions were not verified, and the first process-pool tests did not force lock contention.
attempted_fixes: Added a monotonic generation and previous-snapshot hash to the canonical envelope.
Added an independently replaced anchor that records the highest confirmed generation and hash.
Rejected catalog deletion, same-generation divergence, rollback, missing non-initial anchors, and non-forward anchor recovery.
Reused the hardened private-directory ACL, held-handle, and Windows write-through replacement primitives.
Added synchronized process starts and a real held-lock timeout test.
expected_behavior: The local single-writer catalog distinguishes initialization from deletion, detects an older valid snapshot, and serializes genuinely overlapping processes inside a private directory.
reproduction_commands: python -m pytest tests/ingestion/test_revision_catalog.py -k 'deletion or rollback or lock_is_held' -q
root_cause: A self-checksummed file proves internal consistency but cannot distinguish first use, deletion, or replay of an older self-consistent file; permissions and concurrency also needed executable proof.
security_impact: Without the fix, local loss or rollback could erase replay and tenant-ownership evidence, and weak concurrency tests could overstate serialization assurance.

actual_behavior: The first G6 RED collection failed during import because app.indexing.computation_cache did not exist.
attempted_fixes: Added strict stage artifact, key, envelope, and persistent cache models before enabling any executor behavior.
Kept the import failure JUnit as RED evidence.
expected_behavior: The new cache contract has an executable RED witness before production implementation exists.
root_cause: Intentional RED-first implementation order.
security_impact: None; no cache implementation was present and no artifact was accepted.

actual_behavior: A frozen Pydantic request changed with model_copy could bypass field validation and reach cache path construction.
attempted_fixes: Reconstructed every cache request and payload through model_dump plus strict target-model validation.
Added a regression that an empty tenant copied into a validated key fails before the cache root is created.
expected_behavior: Every value crossing the persistent cache boundary is revalidated even if it is already a model instance.
root_cause: Frozen models prevent normal assignment but model_copy is a trusted construction API and does not re-run every validator by default.
security_impact: Without boundary reconstruction, malformed identity data could influence local cache selection.

actual_behavior: A failure after cache atomic replacement was initially reported as an ordinary publish failure even though the new immutable entry could already exist.
attempted_fixes: Tracked whether atomic replacement completed.
Introduced cache_commit_outcome_unknown after replacement.
Required exact retry to load and return REUSED.
Added orphan cleanup and post-replace fault injection.
expected_behavior: Pre-replace failure is definitely uncommitted; post-replace failure requires idempotent confirmation retry.
root_cause: The first exception handler did not distinguish failures before and after the publication linearization point.
security_impact: Bytes remained immutable, but callers could not choose the correct retry behavior.

actual_behavior: Two intermediate test edits accidentally moved an embedding assertion and a materializer return into unrelated scopes, producing misleading failures.
attempted_fixes: Restored each assertion to its owning embedding test.
Restored DuplicateMaterializer and StaleDocumentMaterializer return paths.
Reran the focused suite before changing production behavior.
expected_behavior: A failing test must identify production behavior rather than malformed fixture control flow.
root_cause: A manual patch matched a repeated context block and placed lines after the wrong function boundary.
security_impact: No production defect; acting on the false signal could have weakened correct cache or governance code.

actual_behavior: The first computation artifact_set_id bound stage cache references but not the complete final governed documents and chunks.
attempted_fixes: Added governance_sha256, documents_sha256, chunks_sha256, and embeddings_sha256.
Included materializer and governance component fingerprints in pipeline identity.
Added a regression where a governance projection changes document/chunk hashes and artifact_set_id while equal vectors retain the same embedding payload hash.
expected_behavior: A computation artifact ID changes whenever any final governed output consumed by G7 changes.
root_cause: The initial manifest treated cache artifact references as sufficient provenance even though target governance materialization occurs after cache lookup.
security_impact: G7 could have received the same artifact ID for different authorization-bearing document/chunk projections.

actual_behavior: The first base-index binding proposal allowed the caller to supply both the claimed base manifest and the checksum that allegedly authenticated it.
attempted_fixes: Removed caller-created BaseIndexBinding from G6.
Required the exact base catalog for non-empty plans and reconstructed the G5 plan for equality.
Deferred authoritative immutable base IndexManifest loading and verification to G7, where it is actually consumed.
expected_behavior: G6 verifies catalog computation lineage without pretending that caller-supplied checksums authenticate an index manifest.
root_cause: Checksum consistency was incorrectly treated as authority even though object and checksum came from one trust domain.
security_impact: A forged sidecar could have created false provenance if G7 later trusted the G6 claim.

actual_behavior: The first cache operation validated the root path but did not hold its directory identity for the complete read or write transaction.
attempted_fixes: Held the private root and its ancestors with no delete sharing on Windows or a directory descriptor on POSIX.
Captured and rechecked root identity around every operation.
Retained per-entry open-handle versus current-path identity checks.
expected_behavior: Cache operations use one stable private directory identity from validation through completion.
root_cause: Path validation and path use were separate operations without a held directory identity.
security_impact: A replaceable root could redirect otherwise validated cache reads or publication.

actual_behavior: The executor initially compared only the set of source identities and target catalog hash; a recomputed, schema-valid plan could still name the wrong target revision or classification.
attempted_fixes: Compared every plan item with the target source head, revision, tenant, region, deletion state, and allowed reason.
Required non-empty plans to equal a deterministic plan rebuilt from the exact base and target catalogs.
expected_behavior: A valid model and plan hash cannot substitute for deterministic base-to-target semantics.
root_cause: Canonical self-hash validation proved internal consistency but not agreement with the authoritative base/target snapshots.
security_impact: Incorrect change classification could have produced misleading reuse provenance.

actual_behavior: A ComputationCacheError raised in a Windows worker could not be unpickled by the parent because RuntimeError stored one formatted argument while the subclass constructor required code and message.
attempted_fixes: Added an explicit __reduce__ that reconstructs the exception from code and message.
Reran synchronized four-process publication.
expected_behavior: Concurrent worker failures preserve their typed cache error across the Windows spawn boundary.
root_cause: Default exception pickling replays exc.args, which did not match the custom constructor signature.
security_impact: The cache still failed closed, but the parent lost the real failure classification and the process pool became broken.

actual_behavior: A new plan check required tombstone_retained previous_revision_id to equal target_revision_id, rejecting a valid already-deleted source when the planning base was empty.
attempted_fixes: Restricted equality to reason_code unchanged.
Kept target head, deleted state, tenant, region, and reason validation for retained tombstones.
Added explicit zero-artifact tombstone regression.
expected_behavior: A tombstone in an empty planning base is retained with no live artifacts and does not require a previous base revision.
root_cause: The unchanged-source base equality rule was generalized to tombstones even though retained_tombstone also describes a deleted target absent from the base.
security_impact: No deletion leaked, but a valid deleted target could not be computed.

actual_behavior: A post-review optimization removed parser/normalizer/chunker provenance from downstream keys and expected embedding hits after those components changed.
attempted_fixes: Re-read the approved R2-S7 cache contract.
Restored parser and normalizer to chunk keys.
Restored the complete parser/normalizer/chunker/config digest to embedding keys.
Changed downstream expectations to misses and retained the RED/GREEN evidence.
expected_behavior: Every affected downstream entry misses when parser, normalizer, chunker configuration, embedding model, dimension, or tenant changes.
root_cause: An advisory reuse-maximization suggestion was applied without rechecking the already approved conservative invalidation protocol.
security_impact: The omitted provenance violated the accepted correctness boundary and could make future behavior changes reuse stale downstream work.

actual_behavior: The first 100-source ratio test used 120 durable catalog transactions plus hundreds of private cache files and exceeded three minutes without producing a result.
attempted_fixes: Terminated only the identified pytest parent and child processes.
Kept durable catalog and persistent cache behavior in their dedicated tests.
Built the ratio input through the same strict in-memory ledger/revision snapshot models.
Used an in-memory cache test double only for call-count isolation and reran in 1.23 seconds.
expected_behavior: The 0/1/5/20 percent matrix measures selective callback correctness without mixing catalog fsync and ACL hardening into its result.
root_cause: One unit test combined persistence durability, private filesystem enforcement, corpus construction, and compute-reuse counting, so unrelated I/O dominated the intended assertion.
security_impact: No product impact; retaining the test would make routine regression impractical and invite skipped coverage.

actual_behavior: The first non-empty governance-update fixture fixed ingested_at to the initial revision time, so the executor correctly rejected the second revision as a stale document binding.
attempted_fixes: Changed the fixture materializer to use revision.occurred_at.
Kept the production equality check so nondeterministic or stale timestamps cannot enter artifact identity.
expected_behavior: Each materialized target document binds the exact deterministic timestamp of its current revision.
root_cause: The original single-revision fixture constant was reused after the test gained a second revision.
security_impact: No production defect; the strict check prevented stale observation time from being accepted.

actual_behavior: An existing cache entry was considered reusable when the loaded Pydantic payload compared equal to the requested payload, even if their canonical JSON bytes and SHA-256 differed, as with -0.0 and 0.0.
attempted_fixes: Kept full schema/checksum validation of the stored entry.
Compared the exact stored canonical envelope bytes with the requested canonical envelope bytes before returning REUSED.
Added a signed-zero regression that must return cache_key_collision.
expected_behavior: An immutable cache key may be replayed only with byte-identical canonical content and must return the hash of the bytes actually stored.
root_cause: Python numeric equality is coarser than canonical serialization identity.
security_impact: The caller could receive a payload hash different from the bytes on disk, breaking deterministic provenance and replay.

actual_behavior: IncrementalComputationResult accepted documents, chunks, or embeddings that did not match its self-consistent computation manifest.
attempted_fixes: Added a cross-field model validator that recomputes final artifact hashes.

Validated document/chunk counts, canonical document bindings, chunk-to-document membership, indexable chunk-to-embedding order, unique embedding chunk IDs, vector dimensions, and embedding binding counts.
Added deserialization regressions for changed governance fields and vector shape.
expected_behavior: A deserialized computation result is rejected unless its actual final artifacts exactly match its manifest.
root_cause: The manifest validated its own artifact_set_id, but the outer result model did not bind those claims back to its artifact tuples.
security_impact: A later G7 deserializer could otherwise accept artifacts different from the manifest it planned to verify or publish.

actual_behavior: total_wall_seconds was captured before final IncrementalComputationResult construction and cross-field validation, excluding work the caller must wait for.
attempted_fixes: Constructed and fully validated a provisional result first.
Captured total wall time after that validation.
Replaced only the measurement field with a freshly validated final measurement object.
Added an injected 50 ms result-validation delay and compared internal time with an external call timer.
expected_behavior: Successful-run total wall time includes final result construction and validation, excluding only negligible final measurement replacement and return.
root_cause: The timer stopped at the end of compute work rather than at the successful public return boundary.
security_impact: No artifact corruption, but performance evidence would systematically under-report successful call latency.

actual_behavior: The invalidation suite changed implementation/model digests but did not explicitly exercise parser semantic version, normalizer semantic version, model identifier, dimension, and tenant across the complete executor.
attempted_fixes: Added direct model-identifier and dimension cache-key checks.
Added an end-to-end matrix using accepted revision provenance for parser/normalizer version changes.
Added complete tenant namespace, model identifier, and embedding dimension runs with stage-specific hit/miss assertions.
expected_behavior: Every field named in the frozen 7.4/G6 invalidation contract has executable miss evidence at the cache or full executor boundary.
root_cause: Earlier tests inferred behavior from model fields and digest changes instead of executing every approved invalidation dimension.
security_impact: Implementation appeared correct, but incomplete evidence could conceal a future key-construction regression.

actual_behavior: The first G7 pytest command failed all 11 fixtures before product code because the nested relative basetemp parent did not exist.
attempted_fixes: Confirmed every traceback had the same pytest mkdir origin.
Created only the D-drive project-local .private/lifecycle/G7_20260726 parent.
Reran the identical focused command and obtained real product-test results.
expected_behavior: G7 tests use a D-drive private basetemp and reach product code.
root_cause: Pytest creates the selected basetemp leaf but did not recursively create the missing custom parent chain on this Windows invocation.
security_impact: No product impact; no project artifact was written to C drive.

actual_behavior: Rollback restored the pointer and query result, then failed while constructing its audit event because the precomputed hash used +00:00 while Pydantic canonical JSON emitted Z.
attempted_fixes: Kept the rollback pointer and query assertions.
Constructed an unhashed model without validation.
Computed event_sha256 from the model's final mode=json representation.
Reran delete and rollback end to end.
expected_behavior: Rollback audit hashes are computed from the exact canonical representation later validated and persisted.
root_cause: The hash producer hand-serialized datetime instead of hashing the validated model's JSON representation.
security_impact: The pointer had already rolled back but the local audit record was absent; fixed before acceptance.

actual_behavior: Parser, normalizer, and embedding injection errors were converted into ordinary business failure codes, hiding the exact injected checkpoint.
attempted_fixes: Kept business callback exceptions mapped to bounded IncrementalComputationError codes.
Moved checkpoint calls immediately before, but outside, callback exception wrappers.
Reran the 14 by 10 failure matrix and successful retries.
expected_behavior: A deterministic fault injector preserves the named checkpoint identity while real callback failures retain bounded domain errors.
root_cause: Checkpoint execution was initially placed inside the same try block as the production callback it observed.
security_impact: No pointer mutation occurred, but failure evidence could not distinguish injected infrastructure failure from parser/model failure.

actual_behavior: A profile binding edit accidentally added profile_id to _strict_inputs instead of _lifecycle_manifest, causing 22 G7 tests to fail at one shared TypeError.
attempted_fixes: Grouped failures by identical first product frame instead of treating them independently.
Moved the parameter to the function that constructs publication identity.
Reran focused and related suites.
expected_behavior: profile_id participates in publication identity and does not change strict G6 input validation.
root_cause: A context-based patch matched the earlier pipeline parameter list rather than the lifecycle builder signature.
security_impact: No artifact was published; every call failed before filesystem mutation.

actual_behavior: The first parent-child regression fixture used child_size 24 with the default overlap 80 and was rejected by the existing ChunkerConfig invariant.
attempted_fixes: Preserved the production overlap invariant.
Set the fixture overlap to 8, below the active child size.
Reran parent-child publication and runtime loading.
expected_behavior: The fixture uses a legal parent-child configuration and tests split-artifact order rather than configuration rejection.
root_cause: The fixture overrode child_size without overriding the inherited fixed-mode overlap.
security_impact: No product impact; strict configuration validation prevented an ambiguous chunk layout.

actual_behavior: Broad and full Windows runs intermittently failed at directory rename publication in ingestion, index, security-evaluation, and load-profile writers; the first full run had 3 failures and 19 setup errors, the second and third each had one remaining call-site failure.
attempted_fixes: Reproduced the EML rename denial repeatedly under a D-drive test root.
Added two business-path regressions for initial staging and staged-to-quarantine publication.
Extracted app/filesystem.py atomic_directory_move instead of duplicating retries.
Restricted retry to Windows winerror 5 while source remains a directory and target remains absent.
Kept FileExistsError and all other permission or I/O failures immediate.
Migrated ingestion, index store, G7 snapshot, security dataset/index/run writers, general evaluation writer, agent evaluation, chunking ablation, and load-profile publication.
Updated old fault-injection tests to patch the shared move boundary and reran the complete repository.
expected_behavior: A complete staging directory is atomically published despite a short Windows sharing denial, without hiding target collision, permanent permission failure, source loss, or non-Windows errors.
reproduction_commands: python -m pytest tests/indexing tests/retrieval tests/ingestion tests/lifecycle tests/security -q
root_cause: Several modules performed a single raw Path.rename/os.rename immediately after durable staging writes. On this Windows host an external sharing/ACL timing window intermittently returned WinError 5; the exact external holder was not identified. Publication policy was also duplicated, so fixing one call site left others vulnerable.
security_impact: The failures did not mutate active.json or publish partial directories, but they caused nondeterministic availability and made complete-suite evidence unreliable.

actual_behavior: The first G8 preview sketch returned a final-looking ChangePlan for a new UPSERT even though no file had been admitted or parsed.
attempted_fixes: Traced every ChangePlan field back to G3-G6 inputs.
Separated exact preview from proposal preview.
Added a model invariant that forbids a proposal carrying a final plan or an exact result without one.
expected_behavior: A new or changed UPSERT preview reports materialization_pending and cannot claim an asset, parser identity, target catalog hash, plan ID, or executable ChangePlan.
root_cause: The design confused a deterministic proposed transition with a fully materialized executable plan. Parser and normalized-content identities do not exist before admission.
security_impact: No production endpoint had shipped, but the misleading result could have caused an operator to approve a plan whose bytes and parser outputs were never validated.

actual_behavior: An invalid materialization request was initially able to create the catalog directory and lock before validation rejected it.
attempted_fixes: Kept materialization validation outside the catalog transaction.
Added a regression that checks the complete root remains absent.
Reran revision catalog and operator suites.
expected_behavior: Invalid event/materialization combinations fail before creating catalog directories, locks, snapshots, or anchors.
root_cause: Validation had been placed after entering the persistent catalog lock, whose preparation legitimately creates private state.
security_impact: The invalid request could not enter catalog history, but it violated the no-side-effect rejection contract and left misleading operational files.

actual_behavior: The first lifecycle API request reached tracing with an unregistered span name and returned 500 before the operator service could run.
attempted_fixes: Added the five bounded lifecycle span names to the tracing allowlist.
Added lifecycle route templates to the secure metrics allowlist.
Reran API, metrics, tracing, and service-profile tests.
expected_behavior: Every exact operator route has an allowlisted low-cardinality metric template and trace span before it is exposed.
root_cause: The endpoint was registered before its bounded observability vocabulary was added to the existing fail-closed allowlists.
security_impact: The fail-closed trace policy prevented uncontrolled labels, but the route was unavailable until the allowlists were updated.

actual_behavior: Rollback could replace active.json successfully and then fail while appending the audit record, leaving the caller with an ordinary error despite the visibility change.
attempted_fixes: Persisted a canonical rollback intent before pointer replacement.
Changed the audit JSONL update to bounded atomic replacement.
Added deterministic reconciliation for target-active, source-active, and conflicting pointer states.
Mapped the post-pointer case to activation_outcome_unknown.
expected_behavior: Pre-pointer failure leaves the pointer unchanged; post-pointer audit failure preserves recoverable intent and reports an explicitly unknown activation outcome.
root_cause: The G7 rollback protocol treated pointer replacement and local audit append as though they had one failure outcome despite being separate durable writes.
security_impact: An old index could become visible without the expected local audit row until manual investigation. The intent protocol now makes recovery deterministic and observable.

actual_behavior: The production lifecycle materializer rejected EML after restart, while directly reusing parse_staged_email would have republished attachment assets on every cache miss.
attempted_fixes: Kept G4 parse_staged_email for first acceptance.
Added a bounded read-only root-body parser that reuses MIME validation without publication or quarantine writes.
Bound the stdlib-email parser fingerprint to email_parser.py.
Compared every staged asset byte and mtime before and after restart parsing.
expected_behavior: First EML acceptance publishes each child through G3 exactly once; restart or cache loss reconstructs the same root ParseResult without changing any asset.
root_cause: The only existing safe EML entry point combined pure MIME parsing with child-asset publication, so it was unsuitable as a repeatable computation-cache callback.
security_impact: Blind reuse would have duplicated child lineage and exhausted event budgets; rejecting EML instead made a supported enterprise source unavailable. The split now preserves both safety and restartability.

actual_behavior: Initial Ollama runtime validation accepted several identity and vector ambiguities: malformed exact digest could fall back to an alias, booleans/non-finite values could enter vectors, callback dimension or model identity could drift, and requests could follow redirects.
attempted_fixes: Selected an exact model entry before validating its digest.
Rejected booleans, strings, NaN, infinity, empty, oversized, and dimension-changing vectors.
Captured the model identifier at runtime creation.
Normalized localhost to literal IPv4 and disabled HTTP redirects.
Added 33 fake-transport tests with no network access.
expected_behavior: The cache fingerprint binds the exact local model digest and dimension used by every finite numeric embedding request, with no proxy or redirect egress.
root_cause: The first factory validated only the nominal response shape and initial URL, not the complete identity and transport invariants required by persistent embedding cache keys.
security_impact: An ambiguous or drifting model could poison cache identity; a redirect could leave the intended local boundary. All cases now fail closed before artifact publication.

actual_behavior: The first operation-lock wrapper could misclassify an OSError or TimeoutError raised after lock acquisition as a lock-acquisition failure.
attempted_fixes: Tracked whether the lock context had yielded.
Mapped only pre-acquisition timeout or filesystem errors to lifecycle_operation_busy or lifecycle_operation_lock_failed.
Allowed post-acquisition exceptions to reach their narrow business mapper.
Reran operator and fault suites.
expected_behavior: Only lock acquisition failures receive lock error codes; business failures after acquisition retain their own stable category.
root_cause: The exception handler surrounded both context-manager acquisition and the complete business operation without distinguishing whether the lock had already been acquired.
security_impact: State remained protected, but an incorrect retry recommendation could cause unsafe operator behavior or obscure a storage incident.

actual_behavior: The first complete G8 repository run passed 2260 tests but failed the exact public trusted-identity result comparison after lifecycle routes changed three identity-bound source files.
attempted_fixes: Reran the single exact comparison with verbose output.
Generated a candidate only through scripts.eval_trusted_identity.
Compared contract ID, matrix verdict, case count, and changed source hashes.
Replaced the public derived result and reran identity plus complete repository suites.
expected_behavior: The committed trusted-identity evaluation exactly recomputes from the frozen 20-case matrix and current identity-bound source bytes.
root_cause: G8 correctly modified exact route policy, app registration, and service-container composition, all intentionally bound by the R2-S5 source contract, but the derived public result had not yet been regenerated.
security_impact: The security cases remained 20 of 20 passing, but stale evidence would have made the public repository unverifiable. The final result now binds the current source contract.

actual_behavior: The first G9 change batch passed ACL groups on a DELETE transport event; strict canonical SourceEvent validation rejected the batch before lifecycle execution.
attempted_fixes: Compared OperatorSourceEventInput with the canonical SourceEvent operation invariants.
Required non-empty ACL groups for UPSERT and prohibited ACL groups for DELETE in the transport model.
Removed ACL groups from the canonical G9 DELETE fixture.
Added a transport regression that fails before business execution.
expected_behavior: The operator transport rejects operation-specific ACL mistakes before source admission or catalog execution and exactly matches canonical SourceEvent semantics.
root_cause: The G8 transport schema checked only the generic tuple shape, while the downstream canonical event model owned the operation-specific ACL rule.
security_impact: The request failed closed before durable mutation, but inconsistent boundary validation produced a late schema failure and an unreliable operator contract.

actual_behavior: The first public G9 summary included catalog, ChangePlan, and publication hashes from one run; a fresh isolated E2E run produced different values and failed exact public-summary comparison.
attempted_fixes: Compared two clean run outputs field by field.
Traced the first divergence to intentionally random secure-staging asset IDs.
Kept exact retry plan and publication equality inside one accepted state.
Replaced cross-run random-derived fields with stable query fingerprints, counts, and Boolean lifecycle invariants.
Added a strict summary model, canonical-byte comparison, sanitization checks, and SHA-256 bindings.
expected_behavior: Public evidence is reproducible only over stable inputs and invariants; random security identities are neither published nor claimed equal across fresh runs.
root_cause: The initial evidence design confused deterministic replay in one durable state with deterministic identities across independently randomized secure admission runs.
security_impact: No product data was exposed, but publishing the old summary would have made a false reproducibility claim and encouraged weakening random asset identity.

actual_behavior: The first G9 public audit reported one machine-specific absolute path finding in the bundle loader because the detector source contained the literal Windows user-root marker it was designed to reject.
attempted_fixes: Confirmed the finding identified detector source rather than fixture or runtime data.
Preserved the exact runtime marker by constructing the Windows separator byte without storing the contiguous absolute-path literal.
Updated the sanitization regression the same way.
Reran focused tests and the complete public audit.
expected_behavior: The repository audit reports zero private paths while the bundle loader still detects the prohibited Windows user-root byte sequence at runtime.
root_cause: The repository scanner is intentionally lexical and cannot infer that a path-shaped literal is a denial marker rather than leaked data.
security_impact: No private value was present, but accepting a noisy audit would weaken the zero-finding release gate. Runtime detection remains equivalent after the source representation change.

actual_behavior: Independent review reproduced that OperatorSourceEventInput accepted traversal paths, invalid media types, naive timestamps, duplicate ACL groups, and control characters; to_source_event then raised an unmapped ValidationError after request validation.
attempted_fixes: Added five RED transport cases and an API 422 boundary case.
Extracted a strict event-template model only for unresolved bundle revision references.
Made concrete OperatorSourceEventInput preflight the complete canonical SourceEvent contract.
Kept DELETE expected-revision mandatory on every actual operator request.
expected_behavior: Every concrete CLI/API event satisfies the complete canonical SourceEvent contract during request validation and cannot reach business execution with a latent Pydantic failure.
root_cause: The G8 transport model duplicated only projection and operation-shape checks instead of reusing SourceEvent validators; conversion occurred outside the mapped business-error boundary.
security_impact: An authenticated malformed request could return an internal 500 rather than a bounded 422 and reached later than the intended security boundary. No durable state was written in the reproduction.

actual_behavior: Independent review embedded a non-fictional address in a Base64 text body, updated the canonical asset/event hashes, and the bundle loader accepted it because identity scanning inspected only raw transfer-encoded bytes.
attempted_fixes: Added a RED hash-valid Base64 fixture.
Exposed bounded read-only decoded-surface inspection from the production G4 MIME parser.
Scanned parsed headers and every transfer-decoded leaf payload with the same fictional marker/domain policy.
Expanded the email matcher to reject single-label and address-literal domains as well as public dotted domains.
expected_behavior: Every raw and transfer-decoded email header, body, attachment, and nested message surface uses only the fictional example.invalid identity domain.
root_cause: The initial public-bundle policy treated the EML container as plain UTF-8 text and did not apply the already available bounded MIME transfer decoder before identity scanning.
security_impact: A public fixture author could unintentionally commit a real address in encoded MIME content while the fictional-identity verifier reported success. The corrected loader fails before returning events.

actual_behavior: Independent review showed that the loader resolved an asset path before _read_regular_file checked is_symlink, so a final or intermediate link to another in-bundle file could become invisible to the link check.
attempted_fixes: Added an internal-link regression that runs where the local OS permits link creation.
Walked every original path component with lstat before resolution.
Rejected any symbolic link and any non-directory parent.
Kept final descriptor identity, no-follow, link-count, size, and mutation checks.
expected_behavior: The bundle loader rejects every symbolic link in the original asset path before opening or resolving its target, even when the target remains inside the bundle.
root_cause: Path containment and link rejection were ordered incorrectly: resolve proved target containment but erased evidence that the caller supplied a link.
security_impact: External path escape was still rejected, but an in-bundle link violated the promised immutable regular-file input policy and weakened path identity evidence.

actual_behavior: The first E2E replay check proved four REPLAYED receipts and unchanged admitted asset bytes but did not compare the replay-built index artifacts or query behavior with the initial target.
attempted_fixes: Loaded and strict-validated both lifecycle manifests.
Compared target catalog, documents, chunks, embeddings, document IDs, indexed/parent chunk IDs, and computation order hashes.
Computed the same fixed-query fingerprint against the replay target and required exact equality.
expected_behavior: Restart replay preserves both admission state and the semantic index/query projection of the initial accepted target.
root_cause: The initial test equated event idempotency and unchanged asset storage with deterministic downstream reconstruction; those are related but separate invariants.
security_impact: No known mismatch occurred, but a regression in restart parsing, chunk order, or embedding evidence could have passed the weaker test.

actual_behavior: The manifest declared expected_source_key_in_initial for the fixed query, but validation and E2E code ignored it and hard-coded the vendor source identity separately.
attempted_fixes: Added a RED manifest case pointing the query to a missing source.
Required every fixed query to bind exactly one initial UPSERT source.
Added a typed expected_initial_event lookup.
Derived the E2E document identity and deletion source checks from the manifest binding.
expected_behavior: Changing the manifest query-source binding either changes the exercised source or fails strict manifest validation; no parallel hard-coded source identity exists.
root_cause: The field was documented as a contract but had no consumer; the test recreated the same fact as a string literal.
security_impact: This was evidence-integrity risk rather than direct data exposure: a manifest edit could silently stop describing the test that reviewers believed it drove.

actual_behavior: The first public summary assigned deleted_residual_count=0 as a literal after checking only active documents, indexed chunks, and retrieval hits; parent chunks and explicit BM25/FAISS/source mappings were not counted, and the name could imply physical deletion from history.
attempted_fixes: Captured the deleted source's initial indexed and parent chunk IDs.
Computed a named residual set from active documents, parent/indexed chunks, chunk-index-backed BM25 and FAISS rows, live source bindings, and retrieval hits.
Required the computed set to be empty.
Renamed the public field active_index_deleted_residual_count to exclude immutable history, tombstone, catalog, asset, and cache retention from the claim.
expected_behavior: The public zero is calculated from all source-addressable structures in the changed active index and is explicitly not a claim of physical deletion from historical audit stores.
root_cause: The test used several individual assertions but serialized a constant summary value and did not name the storage scope of the zero-residue claim.
security_impact: The changed active index was clean in observed runs, but the old evidence could overstate erasure guarantees and miss a parent/index row regression.

actual_behavior: The first post-review complete run failed an evaluation-writer retry test because one injected Windows sharing denial plus one real transient denial produced three move attempts while the test required exactly two.
attempted_fixes: Confirmed publication completed and the artifact was valid.
Compared the assertion with the production primitive's frozen eight-attempt bound.
Updated directory-publication integration tests to require the injected-failure lower bound and the production retry upper bound.
Kept the core no-retry cases for collision, WinError 32, and permanent failures unchanged.
expected_behavior: A retry test proves the injected denial was retried, publication succeeded, and attempts stayed within the production bound without assuming the host adds zero transient denials.
reproduction_commands: python -m pytest tests/test_filesystem.py tests/evaluation/test_writer.py tests/ingestion/test_email_parser.py tests/ingestion/test_file_validation.py -q
root_cause: The integration assertion treated a bounded retry policy as an exact call-count contract on a host where real WinError 5 events are part of the supported behavior.
security_impact: No partial or overwritten artifact occurred. The brittle assertion made full-suite evidence flaky and encouraged removing legitimate availability retries.

actual_behavior: The first post-review complete run also failed one four-process cold-start cache test: a process observed an unsafe ACL while another process was simultaneously hardening the newly created cache root.
attempted_fixes: Minimized to the existing four-process same-key test and repeated cold-start runs.
Traced initialization order through _prepare_root, hold_private_directory, and .cache.lock creation.
Moved lock-file creation and acquisition before ACL mutation.
After locking, captured the root identity, hardened through held handles, revalidated lock identity, and serialized both reads and writes.
Ran the exact test 20 consecutive cold-start iterations and the wider cache/publication suite.
expected_behavior: Concurrent first users serialize root hardening, observe one root/lock identity, and converge to one canonical cache entry without an unsafe-ACL observation window.
root_cause: _prepare_root hardened and validated ACLs before .cache.lock existed, so the operation intended to serialize cache access did not serialize the security-sensitive bootstrap phase.
security_impact: The cache failed closed and published no incorrect cross-tenant entry, but concurrent startup could cause avoidable denial of service and unreliable evidence.

actual_behavior: The first cache-lock reorder fixed the four-process writer reproduction but a broader 111-test run exposed five compatibility failures: unlocked readers assumed a prepared root, hard-link taxonomy changed, post-replace injection depended on a third harden call, and one retry test referenced the wrong module constant.
attempted_fixes: Reran the entire computation-cache suite rather than accepting the narrow reproduction.
Serialized read and write paths through the same bootstrap/business lock.
Added a non-mutating flat regular-file structure preflight before ACL hardening.
Confirmed existing or newly published entries by exact bounded bytes inside the held lock instead of recursively reacquiring through public load methods.
Changed post-replace fault injection to inspect target existence rather than call ordinal.
Corrected the unrelated retry assertion reference and reran 111 related tests.
expected_behavior: Lock-order hardening preserves read miss/hit behavior, fail-closed hard-link taxonomy, non-recursive confirmation, and state-based fault injection across the whole cache surface.
reproduction_commands: python -m pytest tests/indexing/test_computation_cache.py tests/test_filesystem.py tests/agent_v2/test_eval_agent_v2_dev.py tests/corpus/test_artifacts.py tests/evaluation/test_writer.py tests/ingestion/test_email_parser.py tests/ingestion/test_file_validation.py -q
root_cause: The initial repair changed the writer lock order without inventorying the direct read path and tests coupled to the old number of hardening calls.
security_impact: All new failures were fail-closed or test-only and occurred before final acceptance. The corrected design uses one serialized root bootstrap for reads and writes and preserves unsafe-entry rejection.

actual_behavior: The first G10 validation pass found that the mutable handoff projection still described the G9 evidence hashes and record counts after new append-only experiment records existed.
attempted_fixes: Kept every G9 prefix anchor unchanged.
Deferred handoff regeneration until all G10 append-only and mutable evidence is final.
Made integrated validation compare the handoff projection against the repository instead of trusting manually estimated counts.
expected_behavior: The final handoff is regenerated from the accepted repository state and its anchors, open failures, evidence hashes, and record counts agree exactly with the underlying files.
root_cause: CODEX_HANDOFF.json is a mutable projection while its append-only files continued to grow; validating it before final closeout necessarily exposes stale hashes and counts.
security_impact: No source or experiment record was altered. The stale projection could mislead a reviewer about which suffix has been accepted, so closeout remains blocked until one final measured rebuild.

actual_behavior: The first G10 lifecycle bundle bound a parser identity that did not match the parser fingerprint preserved in accepted materialization provenance, so exact restart reconstruction could not be proved.
attempted_fixes: Compared bundle parser metadata with production materialization records.
Centralized the benchmark parser identity in _parser_fingerprint and made bundle generation and loading use that exact contract.
Added exact generator and pipeline identity checks to the bundle loader.
expected_behavior: The generated base and target catalogs bind the same parser implementation identity that production materialization and replay validate.
root_cause: The benchmark generator initially constructed parser metadata in more than one place instead of enforcing one exact benchmark materialization fingerprint.
security_impact: The mismatch failed closed before timing. Accepting it would have compared arms whose provenance could not be tied to the frozen materialization semantics.

actual_behavior: A preflight bundle hashed the input document before applying the benchmark's canonical stripped text, oracle token, and sorted set-like metadata projection, while the generated catalog used the projected document, producing an input/catalog identity mismatch.
attempted_fixes: Reduced the mismatch to one derived document.
Defined the benchmark input projection explicitly: stripped text plus the source-specific oracle token and sorted ACL/fact identifiers.
Computed document checksum and normalized-text hash from those exact projected bytes.
Added a test with whitespace and set-like metadata ordering.
expected_behavior: Bundle input identity and materialization compute hashes from the same explicit canonical benchmark projection for every source.
root_cause: The first generator bound the pre-projection input while downstream catalog generation bound the post-projection document.
security_impact: The mismatch was detected before registration. Without the fix, correctness fingerprints could have certified a different input identity from the bundle manifest.

actual_behavior: The first worker design executed baseline and intervention in one process, but Windows peak working-set counters are cumulative for the process lifetime and therefore could not provide independent arm RSS.
attempted_fixes: Rejected the one-process design before preregistration.
Introduced one pair coordinator and two fresh sequential arm-worker processes.
Assigned disjoint sibling roots and alternated AB/BA order.
Bound process order and host identity into every accepted pair.
expected_behavior: Each arm has an independent operating-system peak RSS observation from a fresh process while preserving paired execution on one host.
root_cause: The original design treated process peak RSS as if it reset between sequential functions; the OS exposes a lifetime high-water mark instead.
security_impact: No security boundary changed. The issue would have produced invalid resource evidence, so the design was replaced before any accepted measurement.

actual_behavior: EXP-LC-001 started but base preparation repeatedly hardened and rescanned the entire cache directory for each entry, creating quadratic work; EXP-LC-003 closed the run INCONCLUSIVE before any timed arm row.
attempted_fixes: Stopped the run rather than waiting for misleading timing.
Recorded the negative result and raw status artifacts.
Added a cache transaction that performs one bounded structure and ACL preparation per batch.
Validated existing ACL state and rewrote it only when unsafe.
Preregistered a new experiment under new IDs instead of editing the original protocol.
expected_behavior: Cache preparation is linear in entries, preserves fail-closed structure and ACL checks, and an infrastructure failure closes the registered experiment without a performance conclusion.
reproduction_commands: python -m scripts.benchmark_lifecycle_incremental run --bundle-dir .private/lifecycle/g10-expanded-lifecycle-v1 --run-id g10-paired-20260727-01 --experiment-id EXP-LC-001 --running-id EXP-LC-002 --completed-id EXP-LC-003 --repetitions 10
root_cause: Each stage store entered the public cache operation independently, and every operation recursively hardened all previously created cache entries.
security_impact: The original path remained fail-closed but was operationally unusable at the frozen corpus size. The repair keeps held-directory identity, flat structure, canonical entry, and ACL validation while removing repeated whole-directory mutation.

actual_behavior: The v1 fixed-query set searched generic titles and a repeated phrase, so four of six expected live sources were absent from the exact top-k result even though both arms produced identical target artifacts.
attempted_fixes: Classified query misses as correctness failures rather than dropping the queries.
Added one deterministic source-specific oracle token to each generated document.
Bound every query to the expected source key, document ID, revision, filters, and token.
Added loader rejection for a query without a bound retrieval oracle.
expected_behavior: Every fixed query deterministically retrieves its bound live source under both arms, while deleted-source queries deterministically prove absence.
root_cause: The first oracle assumed semantic similarity was a stable exact-source assertion, but generic text cannot guarantee which equally relevant source occupies top-k.
security_impact: No incorrect benchmark row was accepted. Treating the misses as correctness failures prevented timing from hiding an under-specified retrieval oracle.

actual_behavior: The v2 queries had unique tokens but hard-coded status=active and temporal_scope=current, excluding expected target revisions whose governed status was retired or stale; three live-source checks failed.
attempted_fixes: Inspected the target catalog revision selected for each query.
Derived every filter from the exact expected revision instead of a benchmark default.
Used temporal_scope=all where the oracle intends to address a governed non-current status.
Added loader validation that filters match the expected revision.
expected_behavior: A query's tenant, region, group, department, policy, status, and temporal scope are generated from and validated against the exact target revision it claims to retrieve.
root_cause: The query generator used an application UI default as an oracle filter instead of treating governance metadata as part of the expected retrieval identity.
security_impact: The error was fail-closed and did not bypass ACLs. The corrected oracle verifies that both benchmark arms preserve the exact governed visibility projection for its positive cases.

actual_behavior: During a preflight pair, the variable holding the final pair output path was overwritten by an arm output path; exclusive creation then refused to replace intervention.json, preventing completion without corrupting it.
attempted_fixes: Kept no-overwrite publication enabled.
Separated pair_result_file from arm_result_file variables.
Added path-containment checks for worker result destinations.
Reran the exact pair worker and pair coordinator.
expected_behavior: Arm results and the aggregate pair result are written once to distinct confined paths, and existing files are never overwritten.
root_cause: One local name was reused for two output ownership levels inside the CLI coordinator.
security_impact: Exclusive-write semantics prevented artifact overwrite. The fix also makes pair-directory confinement explicit, preserving raw evidence integrity.

actual_behavior: The first computation metric stopped before transaction finalization and cache ACL synchronization, leaving material target-build work outside the named compute interval.
attempted_fixes: Compared total wall time with the sum of named phases.
Moved the computation timer boundary to include result validation and transaction finalization.
Added a fault-controlled regression test proving final result validation is included.
Updated the preregistered metric text before the replacement experiment was registered.
expected_behavior: The compute phase covers production computation from entry through validated result and transaction finalization so named phases account for complete target-build work.
root_cause: The timer originally described callback computation only, while the G10 contract defines computation as the whole production G6 operation including secure transaction closeout.
security_impact: No correctness or security check was skipped; the problem was measurement completeness. It was fixed before EXP-LC-004 registration.

actual_behavior: After the successful formal run, serializing the completed experiment with a raw decision string emitted a Pydantic enum warning even though the stored value was valid.
attempted_fixes: Confirmed the six append-only experiment records validate.
Converted the summary decision explicitly to ExperimentFinalStatus at the construction boundary.
Added a CLI regression test that treats warning-free typed serialization as the contract.
expected_behavior: The completed experiment is constructed with the declared enum type and serializes without schema warnings.
root_cause: The summary model and experiment model used equivalent string-valued enums, but the closeout constructor passed one model's serialized string into the other model without explicit conversion.
security_impact: The raw artifacts and decision were unchanged. Removing the warning prevents schema drift from being normalized as harmless noise in later evidence runs.

actual_behavior: An early pytest invocation used the host default TEMP and left <host-temp>/pytest-of-user/pytest-2092 with an ACL that still rejects exact recursive cleanup, including an elevated exact-path attempt.
attempted_fixes: Deleted the adjacent pytest-2091 residue successfully.
Verified the exact pytest-2092 path before each cleanup attempt.
Attempted exact-path recursive deletion without broad host-temp enumeration.
Pinned TEMP and TMP to .private/lifecycle/pytest-temp on the project drive for every subsequent Python and pytest command.
expected_behavior: Lifecycle tests write private temporary state only under the project root and leave no new host-system-drive test artifacts.
reproduction_commands: set TEMP and TMP to .private/lifecycle/pytest-temp before every Python or pytest command
root_cause: One earlier test process inherited the host TEMP before the project-drive isolation rule was applied; the resulting test directory has a host ACL state that the current execution token cannot fully remove.
security_impact: This is a local disk-hygiene issue, not a repository leak or runtime boundary bypass. No subsequent lifecycle artifact is written to the host system drive, and the exact residue remains explicitly tracked for owner cleanup.

actual_behavior: The first G10 focused closeout run passed 130 tests and skipped 7 but one Windows held-directory replacement test failed when the fixture's second Path.rename received a real transient WinError 5.
attempted_fixes: Preserved the failing JUnit instead of rerunning silently.
Ran the exact test ten isolated times; all ten passed, ruling out a stable held-handle sharing regression.
Reused the production bounded Windows directory-move primitive for the fixture's two path substitutions.
Injected one deterministic WinError 5 into the replacement move and asserted that the retry occurred before the security code detected identity change and failed closed.
Reran the exact security and filesystem retry tests.
expected_behavior: The test deterministically tolerates only the repository's supported transient Windows directory denial, still performs the hostile path replacement, and still proves that held-directory hardening rejects the replaced path.
root_cause: The security assertion was correct, but its test-only adversarial path swap bypassed the project's bounded Windows rename policy and therefore converted an allowed transient host denial into a flaky release failure.
security_impact: Production hardening never touched the replacement and remained fail-closed. The corrected test now exercises transient filesystem behavior deterministically without weakening the identity-mismatch assertion.

actual_behavior: Independent review found that EXP-LC-006 binds configuration 3517da4c... while the current source computes a different configuration identity because code changed after the run and the measured source was not yet committed.
attempted_fixes: Kept EXP-LC-004 through EXP-LC-006 and their internally consistent raw rows as historical evidence.
Stopped G10 closeout instead of relabelling the old run.
Expanded source provenance and required runner sources to match a Git commit.
Prepared new schema-v2 experiment IDs for a clean rerun.
expected_behavior: The accepted experiment configuration is computed from the exact committed measurement source, and any later measurement-path change requires a new preregistration and run.
reproduction_commands: compute runner_configuration_sha256 for the frozen v3 bundle and compare it with EXP-LC-006 environment
root_cause: The first formal run occurred before the complete G10 source was frozen in Git; a closeout-only script change then changed the measured configuration hash.
security_impact: No raw timing row was altered, but claiming the old result for current code would break provenance and reviewer reproducibility. G10 remains blocked until a new committed-source experiment completes.

actual_behavior: The G10 contract called the baseline a complete cold full rebuild, while the implementation starts both arms from the same accepted base index/catalog and differs primarily by an empty versus populated computation cache.
attempted_fixes: Traced base-template construction, cloning, arm timing, and post-timing query checks.
Renamed the baseline to cold-cache complete target recomputation from the accepted base state.
Specified that raw-file admission, base-template construction, workspace copy, and correctness queries are outside the timed target-build operation.
Restricted the intended claim to local G6 plus G7 target-build pipeline overhead.
expected_behavior: The contract, experiment record, public summary, and resume claim describe exactly the operation inside the monotonic timing boundary.
reproduction_commands: inspect measure_performance_arm timing boundaries and compare them with section 12B of the lifecycle contract
root_cause: The word full was used for a complete immutable target snapshot and then incorrectly expanded into a claim about full source admission from an empty catalog.
security_impact: This was claim-integrity risk rather than a runtime bypass. The corrected wording prevents an interview or public report from overstating measured end-to-end performance.

actual_behavior: The first runner configuration hash listed selected modules and omitted direct or transitive measurement dependencies such as ChangePlan, store, retrieval, metrics, revision catalog, filesystem, and installed package versions.
attempted_fixes: Replaced the selected list with a canonical manifest of every regular app Python source plus the benchmark entrypoint.
Bound source-path list hash, source-tree bytes, requirements.txt, and key installed dependency versions.
Recorded source file count and required all runner sources to match the registered Git commit before execution.
Added a test asserting the formerly omitted modules are in the source manifest.
