expected_behavior: Any code or dependency change that can affect target computation, publication, correctness checks, or measurement changes configuration_sha256 and invalidates the registration.
root_cause: The initial provenance design manually enumerated obvious benchmark modules rather than binding the complete executable source surface and runtime dependency identity.
security_impact: An omitted dependency could change a correctness fingerprint or timing without changing the recorded configuration. The v2 source manifest now makes that drift fail before work creation.

actual_behavior: The first public G10 directory contained only a summary and checksum while its raw artifacts lived under a Git-ignored directory; its validator did not fully cross-check environment/status and measurement identities.
attempted_fixes: Designed a self-contained package with canonical summary, manifest, checksums, copied raw artifacts, and optional dataset metadata.
Added semantic revalidation of environment, terminal status, commands, pair identities, child arm artifacts, and recomputed summary.
Added a standalone verifier that does not read ignored artifact paths or the experiment ledger.
expected_behavior: A reviewer cloning GitHub can verify bytes, provenance, terminal status, preregistered thresholds, every pair, and the recomputed decision using only the public package and repository code.
root_cause: The first exporter treated repository-relative hashes as sufficient even though the hashed raw files were excluded from Git and several bound aggregate files were not semantically cross-validated.
security_impact: No private content was exposed, but external reviewers could not independently reproduce the result and a mismatched environment projection could be republished. This remains open until the new formal package is exported and verified.

actual_behavior: The v3 query oracle had ACL-positive cases only, so exact target/query equality supported metadata equivalence but not the stated claim that retrieval ACL enforcement was correct.
attempted_fixes: Changed ACL-only updates to remove one old group and add one new group without changing content.
Added authorized positive queries plus removed-group, cross-tenant, and cross-region negative queries.
Made any protected-document hit a correctness failure before timing acceptance.
Regenerated the v4 bundle twice and compared all seven files byte for byte.
expected_behavior: Each arm proves the authorized principal can retrieve the target while the removed group, wrong tenant, and wrong region cannot retrieve it.
reproduction_commands: generate expanded_benchmark_lifecycle_v4 twice and compare seven file hashes
root_cause: The first oracle verified that authorized users saw ACL-updated documents but had no denial cases and the ACL update was additive rather than a revocation.
security_impact: No production ACL bypass was found. The flaw was insufficient experiment coverage; v4 now makes an ACL leak invalidate the entire pair.

actual_behavior: The paired summary hard-coded the same numeric thresholds as the preregistration, but the run command did not prove that the record and code still agreed.
attempted_fixes: Added a strict PairedDecisionProtocol model.
Parsed and exact-matched every success and failure threshold before work creation.
Passed the validated protocol into summary computation.
Added a regression that changes 0.75 to 0.76 and verifies registration rejection.
expected_behavior: The decision is computed from the exact preregistered protocol and any missing, extra, or changed threshold blocks execution before timing.
root_cause: Equal literals in two locations were mistaken for an enforced provenance relationship.
security_impact: A post-registration code or record threshold change could have produced a decision while still claiming preregistration. The exact protocol comparison now fails closed.

actual_behavior: Legacy experiment transitions reused registered_at for REGISTERED, RUNNING, and COMPLETED and the completed record bound only five aggregate files, not each pair/arm/command child artifact.
attempted_fixes: Added backward-compatible experiment schema v2 with aware strictly ordered registered, started, and completed timestamps.
Required v2 history to form REGISTERED to RUNNING to COMPLETED parent transitions.
Made successful completion bind every aggregate and per-pair raw file.
Added an automatic register subcommand that freezes identity and threshold fields without manual JSON editing.
expected_behavior: New experiments expose an ordered transition timeline and hash every execution artifact required to audit each individual pair and arm.
root_cause: The first schema modeled immutable preregistration fields and terminal results but not the execution transition timestamps or complete child-artifact ownership graph.
security_impact: Aggregate pairs were internally consistent, but a reviewer could not establish the exact run timeline or independently hash every child command/result. Schema v2 closes both gaps for the replacement experiment.
